item.text:
**Verdict:** mostly yes, but selectively. Putin did empower some capable technocrats and administrators in 2024, especially for war management and macro-stability, while keeping the core circle loyal and politically safe.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level note | IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Putin taps civilian economist to run defence | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-05-13 | https://theprint.in/world/putin-taps-civilian-economist-to-run-defence/2081878/ | Reuters framed Andrei Belousov as a technocratic choice to improve defence spending efficiency and innovation. This is the clearest 2024 case of Putin choosing capability over pure military pedigree in a major portfolio. | 8B.4; 8B.2; 7B.5 |
| Positive | Putin backs the central bank’s tight policy | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-12-20 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-central-bank-keeps-rates-on-hold-after-putins-call-for-balance-3784135 | Putin publicly backed the central bank’s tight policy rather than overruling it. That suggests he was willing to let monetary experts execute stabilization policy under inflation pressure. | 8B.4; 8B.2; 7B.10 |
| Positive | Government will send additional financing to support medical workers in rural areas | Government of Russia | 2024-12-18 | https://government.ru/docs/53769/ | The state extended `Zemsky Doctor`/`Zemsky Paramedic` through 2030, raised compensation, and allowed transfers to retain specialists. This shows Putin’s system trying to staff delivery with capable professionals and keep them in place. | 8B.4; 8B.2 |
| Positive | Putin orders Russian army to grow by 180,000 soldiers | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-16 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-orders-russian-army-to-grow-by-180000-soldiers-to-become-15-millionstrong-3617373 | The army expansion required a large-scale administrative and manpower push, implying confidence in the coercive bureaucracy and its ability to execute the order. It is capability in a war-footing sense, though not necessarily meritocratic. | 8B.4; 8B.3 |
| Positive | Putin clears out deputy defence ministers, appoints his relative | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-17 | https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-clears-out-deputy-defence-ministers-appoints-his-relative-3486871 | Reuters said Putin removed four deputy defence ministers and replaced them with new figures to fight waste and improve war-economy performance. That indicates active use of personnel changes to improve execution capacity. | 8B.4; 8B.2; 8B.3 |
| Positive | Russia’s economy shows solid growth despite Ukraine war sanctions | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-28 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-economy-shows-solid-growth-despite-ukraine-war-sanctions-3591756 | Reuters reported growth, low unemployment, and expansion in multiple sectors, much of it driven by military production. That is evidence that Putin’s chosen managers were capable of delivering output on the war side of the economy. | 8B.4; 8B.3 |
| Negative | Putin appoints Patrushev and Dyumin as Kremlin aides | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-05-14 | https://theprint.in/world/putin-appoints-patrushev-and-dyumin-as-kremlin-aides/2084276/ | Putin elevated long-time security insiders and a former bodyguard while keeping the core Kremlin staff intact. That is evidence that loyalty remained a major filter even when capability was present. | 8B.4; 7B.5; 8B.3 |
| Negative | Russia: Freedom in the World 2024 | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House describes a system of concentrated power, weak accountability, and pervasive corruption. That makes it harder to separate genuine competence from loyalty-protected appointments and weakens confidence in merit-based empowerment. | 8B.4; 7B.5; 7B.9 |
| Negative | Widening military corruption probe | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-05-23 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/two-more-russian-officials-arrested-in-widening-military-corruption-probe-3454644 | The defence apparatus still generated serious bribery and fraud cases. That suggests Putin’s staffing system did not reliably select clean, capable managers across the board. | 8B.4; 7B.9 |
| Negative | Putin lets economically significant entities limit information disclosures | Reuters | 2024-01-29 | https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-lets-economically-significant-entities-limit-information-disclosures-3315001 | Widening secrecy makes it harder to assess whether officials are truly capable or merely protected. It weakens outside scrutiny of the quality of empowered personnel. | 8B.4; 7B.7; 7B.10 |

Search gap: I found strong examples of Putin using capable technocrats in finance, defense, and social-service staffing, but I did not find evidence of a broad meritocratic system. The positive cases are real, yet they sit inside a loyalist structure where political safety still appears to outrank independence.
